newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Consob says Olivetti statement due Friday.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Consob says Olivetti statement due Friday.

text.p: Italy's stock market watchdog Consob said that information technology group Olivetti would be making a statement on Friday morning following a meeting between the group and Consob on its financial accounts.

A Consob spokesman told reporters waiting outside the meeting between officials of Consob and Olivetti that the information technology group would not made a statement this evening, but would make a statement from its Ivrea headquarters in north-western Italy at around 0700 GMT on Friday morning.

Consob earlier on Thursday met Renzo Francesconi a former Olivetti director general who resigned on Wednesday after only six week at the company after he expressed misgivings about the way the company presented its results for the first half of 1996.
The meeting between Consob and Olivetti, which included Olivetti chief executive Francesco Caio was still going on, the Consob spokesman said.
On Tuesday, Olivetti said it made a pre-tax loss for the first half of 1996 of 440.2 billion lire and added that its chairman Carlo De Benedetti was standing down.
